title: Book One · Chapter 104: No Fastest Boat
story:
The children want a race before the project ends.

Miss Wu looks at the blue basin. Then she looks at the six boats on the table. Some are long, some wide. One has a paper sail. Two have no place for a sail at all.

“How will we choose the winner?” she asks.

“Fastest boat,” Leo says.

“Who blows?”

“Everyone blows their own.”

“And everyone blows with the same wind?”

Leo thinks. “We could ask you.”

Miss Wu folds her arms. “I still do not have six mouths.”

They laugh. Ronan wants a race too. Ronan wants the winner's name at the end of the book. Their flat boat does not look fast, but it did well with stones.

“We can ask different questions,” Mei says. “Do we need one prize?” Which carries stones? Which turns easily? Which keeps the top dry?

“Too many winners,” a boy says.

“Perhaps no winner,” she answers.

Ronan wanted a winner. He feels disappointed.

Miss Wu gives the class a few minutes to look at all the models. No more water goes into the basin. They use their pages to explain their tests.

Leo points to the string. The string holds his pieces together. One partner explains the loose first version. Another points to the new, wider strips. All three children speak. Someone has to remind Leo to stop after his part.

Ronan and Mei stand by their flat boat. A younger child is visiting with another teacher. “Can it sail across the real river?” he asks.

“No,” Ronan says. Then he corrects himself. “We do not know. We made it for a basin.”

The child looks disappointed.

“It carries these three stones in the middle,” Ronan adds. He shows the child their drawing. He does not promise it will sail on the river.

Mei lets the child touch a dry spare strip of wood. The child looks closely at the pale grain. He asks no more about a trip across the river.

Everyone finishes looking at the models. Miss Wu asks for a title for the last page. Ronan suggests Our Results. Mei adds And More Tests for Later. “That needs two lines,” Leo says.

They use two lines.

There is no race. After school, Ronan is still a little sorry. He and Leo walk to the corner. Which boy can blow harder? They argue about that.

They stop by a dry wall and try to move a leaf across its top. Leo blows hard. The leaf jumps sideways and falls. Ronan uses a smaller breath. His leaf moves further along the wall. But it started in a different place.

“That was not fair,” Leo says.

“Neither was your wind.”

They fetch another dry leaf and begin again. Now they must choose the rules themselves. Miss Wu is not there to help them. They choose a crack in the wall as the start. They use one leaf between them.

This time Ronan wins by a finger's length. Leo wins the next. Before the third, the wind takes the leaf away.

“The wind wins,” Leo says.

They watch it go into the grass, nowhere near the water. Then they head home, still pleased with their very small race.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- trip across the river＝过河的行程
- spare＝多余备用的
- finger's length＝一指长
- fair＝公平的

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：sail＝船帆；grain＝木纹；crack＝裂痕。

## 读句提示

**Can it sail across the real river?**

它能／驶过／真正的河吗？it是学校模型，问题本身仍未测试。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么全班没有举行一个“最快船”比赛？
2. 两人课后怎样让吹叶子的游戏更公平一些？
